newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: European bunkers tick up, ARA buyers' nerves crack.
newsitem.headline: European bunkers tick up, ARA buyers' nerves crack.

text.p: European fuel oil bunkers ticked up on Friday and a few buyers, more in the ARA market, decided to accept the higher levels and pick up small lots, dealers said.
Rotterdam 380 CST bunkers rose $1 a tonne to $120/$121 fob, reflecting modest gains in the barge market.

Dealers said buyers were clearly fearful of further rises next week and, after delaying purchases for some time, were drawn back into the market. However, although total demand reached an acceptable 10-15,000 tonnes, individual lots were no higher than a few hundred tonnes each.
"Many of the buyers simply cannot wait any longer," one dealer said.

Demand in other parts of northwest Europe and the Mediterranean ports was more muted. Hamburg's rise of about $2 to $123/$124 left few buyers interested. Mediterranean ports were $1/$2 firmer. Business was slack.
"Everyone's postponing until next week when, in all likelihood, the prices will be higher," one dealers said.
Durban supplies were likely to improve next week as one refinery returned from a shutdown of about two weeks.
